subject: syzygy-q44o: syzygy-bpyt.6.5 blob-reader differential over a git object database (AC 3 capture half) and the E2 harness repairs
headCommitNote: merge of PR #595; between base and head the only non-bpyt.6.5 change under packages/ and apps/ is one cap1-core test (barrel-guard.test.ts), so the source diff is the bead's.

subjectDigestsBeforeRun.note: Written before any run (rule 11): per checkout, the commit, tracked-file cleanliness and the sha256 of every source and test file under both src trees and of the three harness files, test files apart from source.

capture.used: a real Git object database built per scenario by the harness (11 scenarios, one sized as the retained Butlers capture: 185 baseline specs, 13 roster butlers; the scale scenario reads 226 sources, 205 items), read through the production gitRunnerFor so git ls-tree -z and git cat-file run as real processes.
capture.whyNotARetainedButlersCapture: [Observed] no retained capture in the repository holds the Git objects a blob reader reads: docs/evidence/smooth-example-live-run-2026-10-03.json and its siblings retain the model output, not the repository. A differential over Butlers needs the registered checkout behind the real P1 authority gate, which is the owner's to point the harness at.
capture.liveMode: NOT RUN. capture-harness.test.ts.txt carries an operator mode (BPYT65_LIVE_REPO, BPYT65_LIVE_REVISION, BPYT65_LIVE_INSTANT) that evaluates the real P1 gate; no Butlers repository body was read in this work and no daemon was contacted. AC 3's "capture" remains met by the object-database stand-in only; the owner may run the live mode and compare with compare_capture.py.

editedAfterRun.what: one header comment sentence (pointed at a README.md that does not exist; now names vitest.differential.config.ts); no code line changed

harness.run: copy the two harness files to apps/three-surface-poc/src/zz-bpyt65-{differential,capture}.test.ts and the config to vitest.differential.config.ts at the root of a checkout (base and head); in each: TMPDIR=<any> BPYT65_OUT=<d.json> BPYT65_CAPTURE_OUT=<c.json> npx vitest run --config vitest.differential.config.ts; then compare_differential.py base head and compare_capture.py base head.

e2Repairs.headerRunCommand: the old header named --project three-surface-poc (no such project filter: the suite is tiered, CONTRIBUTING.md; the unit tier refuses a test that spawns git and the base has no tiers). The header now gives the --config form above, which ran at both commits.
e2Repairs.outputDigests: [Observed] the model rows hash pages whose evaluation-inputs digest names the repository root; the harness put that root under TMPDIR, so every TMPDIR gave a different output sha256 (explains the reviewer's mismatch with the recorded 2026-11-03 digests, which are TMPDIR=/tmp/b65 ones). The root is now BPYT65_FIXTURE_ROOT (default /tmp/bpyt65-fixture-root). With it, two runs per side under different TMPDIRs gave one sha256 each (below). The older record's digests are unchanged and reproduce only under its own TMPDIR.
e2Repairs.subjectDigests: the pre-run file above; the older record's test-file digests postdated its run, and its non-test source digests remain its valid anchor.

differential.expectedDifference: 60 shapes where the fault fires on the second ls-tree: base observation-failed, head observed (one listing)

rule6.note: each mutation of the head output (shape field, extra cat-file, extra ls-tree, revision, missing scenario, mode, second ls-tree kept) made the comparator exit 1; compare_differential.py was mutation-tested by the parent record.

verdict: No unexpected difference. On a real object database, 11 of 11 scenarios give a byte-identical shape record at base and head, the same cat-file count, and the head lists the tree once where base listed it twice. The v1 fixture differential re-ran at the same two commits with the same result (0 unexpected; 60 expected second-listing differences). Live Butlers capture not run (owner).
